questions.question: You are giving a radio report to the receiving hospital. For each item, decide whether it belongs in the report.
choices: The patient’s full name and date of birth
Your opinion of the patient’s lifestyle
The most recent vital signs
The chief complaint
The patient’s age and sex
Your estimated time of arrival
questions.explanation: A radio report is short and gives the hospital what it needs to prepare: your unit, the patient’s age and sex, the chief complaint, key findings, vital signs, treatment and response, and your estimated time of arrival. Names and other identifying details are left off the radio, which others can hear, and are passed on in person or in the written record. Personal opinions about the patient do not belong in any report.

questions.question: What is an emergency medical services (EMS) system?
choices: A coordinated network providing emergency care and transport
The individual ambulance crew assigned to a call
The hospital emergency department alone
The physician’s written standing orders alone
questions.explanation: EMS is an organized system linking responders, care, communication, transport, and other components; an individual crew or service is one component.

questions.question: Which sequence lists the four nationally described EMS provider levels from basic to most advanced?
choices: EMR → EMT → AEMT → paramedic
EMT → EMR → AEMT → paramedic
EMR → AEMT → EMT → paramedic
EMR → EMT → paramedic → AEMT
questions.explanation: The ordered levels are EMR, EMT, AEMT, and paramedic.

questions.question: A candidate passes an EMT certification examination. The destination state still requires an application and screening before licensure. What does the exam result establish?
choices: Evidence of competence, while the remaining state practice requirements still apply
Permission to practice immediately because national certification replaces state licensure
Permission to practice if an employer offers a position before screening
Permission to practice if the candidate stays within BLS skills until licensed
questions.explanation: Certification and state permission to function are separate parts of qualification.

questions.question: Which development is associated with the 1966 report Accidental Death and Disability: The Neglected Disease of Modern Society?
choices: A national call to improve inconsistent emergency care and develop organized EMS
Publication of the first AAOS EMT textbook
Creation of federal EMS development funding through the 1973 EMS Act
Release of the people-centered EMS Agenda 2050
questions.explanation: The White Paper highlighted deficiencies and prompted improvements in modern EMS.

questions.question: Which procedure is associated with basic EMT care rather than the advanced procedures listed for AEMTs or paramedics?
choices: Use of basic airway adjuncts
Peripheral IV therapy
Endotracheal intubation
Cardiac rhythm interpretation with rhythm-specific advanced treatment
questions.explanation: Basic airway adjuncts are included in EMT care in the provider-level overview.

questions.question: At a safe scene, a first-aid-trained bystander offers to help. Before assigning them a patient-care task, what should the EMT establish?
choices: Whether the bystander can perform that task safely
Whether the task will shorten the time on scene
Whether the patient prefers a bystander to perform the task
Whether another bystander has performed the task before
questions.explanation: The task must match this helper’s abilities. Saving time or having patient agreement does not establish the helper’s competence.

questions.question: An agency wants to make EMS more people-centered. Which plan best addresses patients across the care continuum?
choices: Coordinate access, prevention, evidence-based care, and relevant patient records
Prioritize response speed while leaving hospital coordination to receiving staff
Measure success mainly by transport counts and equipment utilization
Expand emergency treatments while keeping prevention separate from EMS
questions.explanation: People-centered care includes accessible, coordinated, preventive, evidence-based services.

questions.question: A physician gives an EMT patient-specific care instructions by radio during a call. Which form of medical direction is this?
choices: Online/direct medical direction
Off-line/indirect medical direction
A standing order
A written protocol
questions.explanation: Live physician instructions by radio or phone are online/direct control.

questions.question: A program uses paramedics, nurses, and physicians to deliver care in the community. Some participating paramedics complete extra preparation for chronic-condition follow-up. How are the two concepts related?
choices: The broader approach is MIH; the specially prepared paramedic role is community paramedicine
The broader approach is community paramedicine; MIH is the individual paramedic qualification
MIH is a new EMS licensure level; community paramedicine is a replacement for EMT training
The broader approach is ordinary emergency transport; the added role is limited ALS certification
questions.explanation: MIH is a community care-delivery approach; community paramedicine is an associated specially prepared role.

questions.question: An agency repeatedly audits patient care, identifies problems, implements improvements, and reviews the results. What is the main purpose of this process?
choices: Improve system performance and reduce errors through CQI
Determine whether each clinician meets initial certification requirements
Issue real-time clinical orders for individual patients
Provide refresher education without evaluating system performance
questions.explanation: CQI evaluates the system and uses findings to improve care.

questions.question: Which activity most directly aims to prevent a motor vehicle crash from occurring?
choices: Teaching community members about avoiding impaired driving
Encouraging seat belt use to reduce injury during a crash
Protecting an injured patient from further movement after a crash
Reviewing the care provided after a crash
questions.explanation: This is primary prevention: teaching people to avoid impaired driving aims to prevent the crash itself. Secondary prevention reduces the effects of an event that occurs, such as seat belts reducing injury during a crash.

questions.question: A required airway device fails the pre-shift check. A replacement is available at the station. What best completes the EMT’s readiness responsibility?
choices: Replace it, verify the replacement, and report the fault
Record the fault and rely on the spare during the next call
Report the fault and leave replacement to the next shift
Repeat the check after the ambulance is dispatched
questions.explanation: Readiness requires usable, checked equipment before it is needed. Reporting the fault supports follow-up but does not itself restore readiness.

questions.question: A frightened patient speaks angrily but remains cooperative and poses no safety threat. Which response best supports the assessment?
choices: Acknowledge the fear and explain the next assessment step
Use brief clinical questions and leave the emotional concerns for the hospital
Ask a relative to answer so the patient can stop talking
Explain the likely diagnosis before asking about the patient’s concerns
questions.explanation: Acknowledging fear and explaining what happens next can support cooperation without making an unsupported diagnosis or bypassing the patient.

questions.question: Which disclosure best fits the EMT’s patient-confidentiality responsibility?
choices: Relevant findings to the clinician accepting the patient’s care
An identifiable call summary to an off-duty colleague who is not involved in care
The same details to a relative solely because they ask
A patient photograph in a closed social group for informal discussion
questions.explanation: Relevant patient findings may be communicated to those treating the patient; unauthorized identifiable disclosures violate confidentiality.

questions.question: Which sequence represents the PDSA improvement cycle?
choices: Plan → do → study → act
Plan → study → do → act
Plan → do → act → study
Do → plan → study → act
questions.explanation: The cycle tests a planned change, studies the result, and then acts on the findings.

questions.question: An EMT follows a known procedure but selects an inappropriate intervention because they do not know a key fact about it. Which error category best fits?
choices: Knowledge-based failure
Rules-based failure
Skill-based failure
An equipment-readiness failure
questions.explanation: The underlying problem is missing information needed for the decision.

questions.question: An EMT knows that a protocol requires a step but intentionally skips it. Which error category best fits?
choices: Rules-based failure
Knowledge-based failure
Skill-based failure
An information-system failure
questions.explanation: The provider fails to follow a known requirement.

questions.question: An EMT knows the correct routine technique but performs it incorrectly while distracted. Which error category best fits?
choices: Skill-based failure
Knowledge-based failure
Rules-based failure
A scope-of-practice limitation
questions.explanation: The error is execution of a known routine task.

questions.question: Which combination best matches the limited ALS skills listed for an AEMT?
choices: IV therapy, supraglottic airways, and a limited number of emergency medications
Basic airway adjuncts, AED use, and medication assistance only
Endotracheal intubation, broad emergency pharmacology, and advanced rhythm treatment
Public CPR, AED use, and immediate care until ambulance arrival
questions.explanation: The course distinguishes limited AEMT ALS from basic EMT care and extensive paramedic ALS.

questions.question: During transport, a patient’s blood pressure fell and mental status worsened before improving after an intervention. What handoff best preserves continuity of care?
choices: Initial findings, the deterioration, the intervention, and the response
The latest vital signs and current mental status
The intervention and the time it was performed
The original complaint and initial vital signs
questions.explanation: The receiving team needs the clinical course and response, not just a snapshot or a treatment list.

questions.question: An agency wants to apply Just Culture after an error. Which review approach fits that goal?
choices: Examine system factors and behavioral choices, balancing learning with fair accountability
Assign the same consequence to every error to ensure consistency
Focus only on the system and exclude any consideration of individual choices
Focus only on the individual to avoid changing established processes
questions.explanation: Just Culture balances fairness, learning, and accountability for behavioral choices.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly distinguishes EMS certification from state licensure?
choices: Competence assessment; permission to practice under state requirements
Permission to practice under state requirements; competence assessment
Employer orientation; permission to practice under state requirements
Competence assessment; authorization for a particular treatment under medical direction
questions.explanation: Certification assesses entry competence; licensure is the state process governing permission to function.

questions.question: An EMT applicant has a disability. Which employment approach maintains both fair access and required job performance?
choices: Consider appropriate modifications while evaluating the ability to perform required job functions
Lower the clinical qualification requirements solely because of the disability
Exclude the applicant before considering how the functions could be performed
Treat a disability as proof that the applicant cannot safely perform any EMT task
questions.explanation: The chapter discusses fair employment and possible modifications while retaining the required functions and qualifications.

questions.question: An EMT moves to a new state. What should they establish before practicing there?
choices: That they meet the destination state’s applicable licensure and practice requirements
That their existing certification covers the same national provider level
That the new employer uses skills familiar from the old service
That their former medical director approves the move
questions.explanation: The destination state’s requirements control permission to practice there.

questions.question: An agency identifies repeated documentation omissions and tests a training change. A follow-up audit is complete. What should happen next?
choices: Study whether the omissions decreased and adjust or sustain the change based on the findings
Continue the change because training attendance alone proves improvement
Select the next training topic without analyzing the audit
Repeat the original training unchanged regardless of the audit findings
questions.explanation: PDSA requires using the measured results to decide what to do next.

questions.question: An EMT follows a written standing order that authorizes care for the patient’s condition. How does this differ from receiving patient-specific instructions by radio?
choices: Standing orders are off-line direction; radio instructions are online direction
Both are online direction because both authorize care
Standing orders are online direction; radio instructions are off-line direction
Written orders authorize care only after a separate physician call on every patient
questions.explanation: Standing orders are part of off-line medical control; live radio or telephone orders are online control.

questions.question: An EMR reaches a patient before the ambulance. Which role fits this provider level?
choices: Give immediate care and support the arriving EMS team without replacing the transporting EMT role
Provide comprehensive advanced rhythm treatment before the ambulance arrives
Function as the ambulance’s primary transport-care provider solely because the EMR arrived first
Establish an IV and give the full range of paramedic medications
questions.explanation: EMRs provide immediate lifesaving care and assist the team; arrival order does not change training or scope.

questions.question: Which combination distinguishes extensive paramedic ALS preparation from the limited ALS skills described for an AEMT?
choices: Endotracheal intubation, emergency pharmacology, and cardiac monitoring
Basic airway adjuncts, AED use, and basic patient assessment
Immediate first-response care while awaiting the transporting team
IV therapy and a limited medication set as the complete advanced skill range
questions.explanation: Paramedic education includes extensive ALS skills; limited IV, airway, and medication preparation characterizes the AEMT level.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly distinguishes the 1971 textbook milestone from the 1973 EMS Act?
choices: The textbook standardized education; the Act supported EMS system funding and development
The textbook established federal EMS funding; the Act standardized EMT course content
The textbook issued practice licenses; the Act certified individual EMT competence
The textbook established physician standing orders; the Act established agency CQI
questions.explanation: The textbook supported education, while the 1973 Act supported development of prehospital systems.

questions.question: What is continuous quality improvement (CQI) in EMS?
choices: An ongoing process of reviewing performance and improving care
The initial process of granting an EMT a license
The process of issuing patient-specific physician orders
The initial course that qualifies a provider for certification
questions.explanation: CQI uses continuing review and improvement to support better care; licensure, medical direction, and initial education have different purposes.

questions.question: A crash still occurs, but a properly worn seat belt reduces the occupant’s injuries. Which prevention category describes that protective effect?
choices: Secondary prevention
Primary prevention
Continuous quality improvement
Medical direction
questions.explanation: Secondary prevention reduces the effects of an event that occurs. Primary prevention aims to stop the event from occurring.

questions.question: An EMT makes a patient’s needs central when coordinating care and communicating concerns to the receiving team. Which professional attribute does this most directly demonstrate?
choices: Patient advocacy
Self-confidence
Time management
Personal appearance
questions.explanation: Patient advocacy means keeping the patient’s needs at the center of care.

questions.question: An EMT manages difficult calls well but has stopped sleeping adequately and seeing friends. Which plan best supports resilience over time?
choices: Protect recovery time, maintain supportive relationships, and use healthy routines
Build resilience mainly by taking more difficult calls
Keep the schedule and use caffeine to replace lost sleep
Reserve self-care changes until job performance declines
questions.explanation: Resilience involves coping and recovering; rest, relationships, and healthy habits support that recovery.

questions.question: What is an infectious disease?
choices: A disease caused by harmful organisms within the body
A disease that necessarily spreads directly from one person to another
A disease that results from a physical injury
A disease defined by a harmful immune response to an otherwise harmless substance
questions.explanation: An infectious disease is caused by harmful organisms within the body. A communicable disease can spread between people or species.

questions.question: Late in a shift, an EMT repeatedly loses focus and nearly falls asleep before driving. What is the best response?
choices: Report the impairment and arrange a safe fatigue-management response
Drink caffeine and begin driving while waiting for it to work
Drive with the window open and rely on the partner to keep talking
Complete the next transport before reporting the fatigue
questions.explanation: Impaired alertness threatens driving and patient-care safety; address the risk before a preventable incident.

questions.question: A pathogen reaches a person through the bite of an infected tick. Which transmission route is involved?
choices: Vector-borne
Indirect contact with a contaminated object
Direct person-to-person contact
Airborne
questions.explanation: A living carrier such as a tick transmits the pathogen.

questions.question: A coughing patient is suspected of having infectious pulmonary tuberculosis. The patient can tolerate a mask and does not need oxygen. Which pairing best provides source control and provider respiratory protection?
choices: Surgical mask on the patient; fit-tested N95 or higher-level respirator on the provider
N95 on the patient; surgical mask on the provider
Surgical masks on both patient and provider
N95 on the provider; omit patient masking because the provider is protected
questions.explanation: Patient masking limits release of infectious particles; a suitable respirator protects the provider from airborne exposure.

questions.question: An EMT expects substantial blood splatter while treating trauma. The patient has no known infectious diagnosis. Which PPE decision best applies standard precautions?
choices: Use gloves and appropriate eye, face, and clothing protection for the anticipated exposure
Use gloves alone until an infectious diagnosis is confirmed
Use gloves and a surgical mask, relying on prescription glasses for eye protection
Choose PPE only after asking whether the patient has hepatitis or HIV
questions.explanation: Standard precautions apply regardless of known diagnosis; the anticipated exposure determines needed protection.

questions.question: Why does wearing an N95 respirator require a respiratory-protection program that includes fit testing?
choices: Filtering material alone is insufficient if air leaks around an unsuitable face seal
Fit testing replaces the need for the correct respirator type
The N95 rating means every wearer has an adequate seal
A surgical mask underneath necessarily corrects a poor fit
questions.explanation: A respirator must both filter particles and fit the wearer appropriately.

questions.question: After removing gloves, an EMT finds visible blood on their hands. A sink and alcohol-based sanitizer are available. Which cleaning method is appropriate?
choices: Soap and water with friction over all hand surfaces, followed by rinsing and drying
Alcohol-based sanitizer rubbed over all hand surfaces until dry
Water rinsing followed by alcohol-based sanitizer
Soap and water applied to the visibly stained areas only
questions.explanation: Visible contamination calls for washing with soap and water. Clean all hand surfaces, including fingertips and between fingers, rather than only the visible stain.

questions.question: Which pair describes two ways a person can acquire immunity to a particular pathogen?
choices: Vaccination and recovery from a previous infection
Wearing gloves and cleaning contaminated equipment
Taking antibiotics and avoiding patient contact
Vaccination and having no symptoms during one exposure
questions.explanation: Vaccination and prior infection can produce pathogen-specific immune protection; neither guarantees lifelong complete protection.

questions.question: A contaminated needle punctures an EMT’s skin. A partner can safely take over care. Which plan best addresses the exposure?
choices: Wash the site, report the exposure, and obtain prompt medical evaluation
Wash the site and obtain the source patient’s test results before seeking evaluation
Finish transport, then wash the site and complete an exposure report
Wash the site and arrange routine follow-up if symptoms appear
questions.explanation: Exposure first aid, reporting, and medical evaluation should be prompt. Source testing may help the evaluation but should not postpone it.

questions.question: A leaking tanker has an unreadable placard. Patients are near the spill. The EMT crew lacks hazardous-material entry training and equipment. What should the crew do first?
choices: Stage safely away from the spill and request trained hazardous-material resources
Approach far enough to read the placard, then select a staging location
Use examination gloves and an N95 to reach the nearest patient before the hazmat team
Park near the patient cluster and prepare treatment while the spill is identified
questions.explanation: Protect responders first, identify hazards from a safe distance, and use trained resources for entry and decontamination.

questions.question: Which inner-to-outer clothing arrangement best manages moisture, insulation, and weather protection?
choices: Moisture-wicking layer → insulating layer → weather-resistant layer
Weather-resistant layer → moisture-wicking layer → insulating layer
Insulating layer → weather-resistant layer → moisture-wicking layer
Moisture-wicking layer → weather-resistant layer → insulating layer
questions.explanation: The inner layer moves moisture away, the middle insulates, and the outer layer resists wind and precipitation.

questions.question: After a death, one family member is silent and another alternates between disbelief and anger without threatening anyone. How should the EMT respond?
choices: Offer honest, calm support and allow each person to express grief differently
Explain that anger must end before they can move to the next stage
Interpret the silent relative’s behavior as definite acceptance
Give a detailed account immediately so both relatives will process the loss in the same way
questions.explanation: Grief reactions can differ and overlap; supportive care does not require a fixed sequence or a single style of grieving.

questions.question: Which pattern best fits the immediate alarm response to stress?
choices: Faster pulse and breathing, dilated pupils, and reduced gastrointestinal blood flow
Slower pulse and breathing, dilated pupils, and increased gastrointestinal blood flow
Faster pulse and breathing, constricted pupils, and increased gastrointestinal blood flow
Slower pulse and breathing, constricted pupils, and reduced gastrointestinal blood flow
questions.explanation: The alarm response increases readiness for action while shifting resources away from digestion.

questions.question: After a traumatic call, an EMT has intrusive memories and nightmares that interfere with work. Which support plan best addresses the ongoing symptoms?
choices: Qualified mental-health assessment, with peer support as appropriate
A facilitated peer-support session as the sole intervention
An operational review focused on the clinical decisions made during the call
A change in shift schedule without mental-health follow-up
questions.explanation: Work-disrupting trauma-linked symptoms warrant qualified assessment. Peer support and schedule changes may help, but do not replace evaluation of persistent symptoms.

questions.question: A critically injured patient asks, “Am I going to die?” The outcome is uncertain. Which response best balances honesty and reassurance?
choices: “Your injuries are serious. We are treating you and getting you further care.”
“You will be fine; there is no reason to worry.”
“I cannot tell you anything until we reach the hospital.”
“Let me explain every possible complication before we continue.”
questions.explanation: Acknowledge seriousness without an unsupported prediction, and explain the care being provided.

questions.question: After a mass-casualty incident, an experienced EMT feels overwhelmed despite performing their assigned tasks correctly. What is the most appropriate interpretation?
choices: Severe incidents can overwhelm normal coping even when clinical performance is sound
Stress proves that the EMT failed to prepare adequately
Correct performance rules out the need for emotional support
A strong immediate reaction by itself establishes PTSD
questions.explanation: Critical incidents can produce major stress in experienced providers; support needs are not determined solely by technical performance.

questions.question: A family member blocks the exit, threatens the crew, and advances toward an EMT. Which action should take priority?
choices: Create distance, disengage when safe, and request law enforcement
Remain beside the patient and continue calm verbal de-escalation
Move closer to the family member to discuss the concern privately
Ask the patient to persuade the family member while assessment continues
questions.explanation: Active threats and a blocked exit require a protective response. Calm communication may continue when safe, but must not keep the crew exposed.

questions.question: Which observation most strongly raises concern for an immediate behavioral safety emergency?
choices: A patient threatens to injure the crew and moves toward them aggressively
A patient reports a past psychiatric diagnosis while calmly requesting help
A relative cries after a loss but remains safe and cooperative
A patient disagrees with the treatment recommendation and explains their reasons
questions.explanation: Threats combined with escalating behavior create an immediate safety concern requiring a protective response.

questions.question: A supervisor makes a preferred shift assignment conditional on an employee agreeing to sexual activity. Which workplace issue is most specifically illustrated?
choices: Quid pro quo sexual harassment
Hostile work environment based only on general offensive comments
Cultural differences in communication
A consensual personal relationship unrelated to employment
questions.explanation: A work benefit conditioned on sexual compliance is the distinguishing feature of quid pro quo harassment.

questions.question: An EMT says ongoing stress is becoming unmanageable and asks where to get help. No immediate danger is reported. Which plan best connects them to support?
choices: Help them access the EAP or qualified mental-health services, with peer support as appropriate
Rely on informal coworker conversations as the complete solution
Suggest changing shifts and postpone referral until errors occur
Refer them only to a fitness program because exercise improves stress
questions.explanation: Employee assistance and qualified mental-health services can provide assessment and ongoing support before safety or functioning deteriorates further.

questions.question: Which exposure is a recognized occupational route for both hepatitis B and HIV?
choices: A puncture from a needle contaminated with infected blood
Breathing the same room air as an infected patient
An insect bite after the insect contacts the patient
Eating food prepared in the same building as the patient
questions.explanation: Infected blood introduced through a sharps injury is a bloodborne exposure route.

questions.question: An EMT finishes care of one patient and is about to assess another. The gloves look clean. Which practice best prevents cross-contamination?
choices: Remove gloves without touching their contaminated exterior with bare skin, clean hands, and use fresh gloves when indicated
Keep the gloves on because visible contamination is absent
Apply hand sanitizer to the gloves and continue to the next patient
Change gloves but omit hand hygiene because the hands were covered
questions.explanation: Gloves must be changed between patients and do not replace hand hygiene; careful removal reduces self-contamination.

questions.question: Why can carbon monoxide exposure impair oxygen delivery even when a person continues to breathe?
choices: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin and interferes with oxygen transport
Carbon monoxide primarily fills the alveoli with mucus
Carbon monoxide immediately destroys the circulating red-cell population
Carbon monoxide protects hemoglobin from releasing carbon dioxide
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds hemoglobin in red blood cells, interfering with the blood’s ability to oxygenate the body.

questions.question: Before a shift, a partner is unsteady and speaks unclearly after taking medication. The cause is uncertain. What is the best response?
choices: Report the observed impairment and arrange a safe staffing response through the agency process
Let the partner drive if the medication was prescribed
Privately suggest using less medication after the shift and proceed normally
Diagnose substance misuse and discuss the suspicion broadly with coworkers
questions.explanation: Address observed safety impairment through the agency process without assuming a diagnosis; prescribed drugs can also impair performance.

questions.question: Coworkers have different beliefs and communication styles. Which approach best supports cultural humility?
choices: Stay curious, reflect on personal assumptions, and communicate respectfully about individual needs
Memorize stereotypes about each group and use them to predict every coworker’s preferences
Require all coworkers to communicate in the most senior EMT’s style
Treat cultural differences as limited to nationality and ignore other backgrounds
questions.explanation: Cultural humility requires ongoing reflection, curiosity, and sensitive communication, rather than assumptions about group membership.

questions.question: An EMT touches a contaminated object and then transfers the contamination to their own mucous membrane. Which route best describes this?
choices: Indirect contact
Direct person-to-person contact
Vector-borne transmission
Foodborne transmission
questions.explanation: The contaminated intermediate object makes this indirect contact.

questions.question: An EMT has finished using a needle and an approved sharps container is within reach. Which action minimizes handling risk?
choices: Dispose of the needle directly in the rigid sharps container without recapping
Recap the needle before placing it in the container to hide the sharp point
Bend the needle before disposal so it cannot be reused
Place it temporarily in a medical-waste bag until other cleanup is complete
questions.explanation: Used needles belong in an approved rigid sharps container without recapping, bending, or unnecessary extra handling.

questions.question: Which pairing correctly identifies stress reactions by their timing?
choices: During the event: acute; after the event: delayed; prolonged repeated stress: cumulative
During the event: delayed; after the event: acute; prolonged repeated stress: cumulative
During the event: acute; after the event: cumulative; prolonged repeated stress: delayed
During the event: cumulative; after the event: delayed; prolonged repeated stress: acute
questions.explanation: The timing distinguishes acute, delayed, and cumulative reactions; timing alone does not diagnose PTSD.

questions.question: A team is arranging a facilitated emotional-support session after a traumatic call. Which agenda would undermine that session’s purpose?
choices: Turning it into a critique of individual clinical errors
Allowing providers to describe their emotional reactions
Using a trained facilitator to support the discussion
Offering private mental-health counseling when group support is unsuitable
questions.explanation: Critical-incident emotional support should not be turned into an operational critique. Performance review and emotional support have different purposes.

questions.question: A rescue operation creates a risk of falling debris and tool-generated fragments. Which gear pairing directly addresses those hazards?
choices: A secure protective helmet plus appropriate goggles and face protection
A surgical mask and an insulating clothing layer alone
Prescription glasses and an unsecured construction helmet
Examination gloves and earplugs as complete protection
questions.explanation: Impact protection and secure helmet fit address debris; goggles or face protection address fragments from tools.
tags: Protective gear matched to the hazard

questions.question: What does resilience mean?
choices: The ability to cope with and recover from distress
The active pursuit of good health
The positive response to a stressor
The negative response to a stressor
questions.explanation: Resilience concerns coping and recovery. Wellness is the pursuit of good health; eustress and distress describe positive and negative stress responses.

questions.question: What makes a disease communicable?
choices: It can spread from one person or species to another
It is caused by any harmful organism, whether or not it spreads
It produces symptoms immediately after exposure
It produces lifelong immunity after one infection
questions.explanation: Communicable describes spread. Infectious describes a disease caused by harmful organisms, which does not by itself establish communicability.

questions.question: What term specifically describes a gradual lessening of compassion and empathy associated with repeated caregiving stress?
choices: Compassion fatigue
An acute stress reaction
A delayed stress reaction
Resilience
questions.explanation: Compassion fatigue is a gradual lessening of compassion over time and is also called secondary stress disorder.

questions.question: After prolonged job stress, an EMT reports exhaustion, cynicism, and declining work performance. Which term best matches this combination?
choices: Burnout
Resilience
An isolated acute stress response
Normal physiologic arousal during a single call
questions.explanation: Burnout combines exhaustion, cynicism, and reduced performance resulting from long-term job stress.

questions.question: An adult requesting to refuse transport correctly states the date and location but cannot explain the risks the EMT has just described. What is the best next step?
choices: Assess understanding further and consult medical direction if capacity remains uncertain
Repeat the orientation questions and accept refusal if the answers remain correct
Obtain a witness signature after repeating the transport recommendation
Ask the accompanying relative to authorize the refusal
questions.explanation: Orientation alone does not establish the ability to make this decision. The patient must understand the relevant consequences; uncertainty needs further assessment and appropriate consultation.

questions.question: An unconscious adult has a life-threatening condition. No authorized decision maker or applicable treatment-limiting order is available. What supports starting necessary emergency care?
choices: Implied consent under the emergency doctrine
Expressed consent inferred from the absence of a refusal
Involuntary consent based solely on unconsciousness
Consent that must first be obtained from a relative
questions.explanation: The emergency doctrine permits necessary care when the patient cannot decide and timely consent is unavailable.

questions.question: After an EMT explains a blood pressure measurement, a capable patient nods and extends an arm. How should this consent be classified?
choices: Expressed consent communicated nonverbally
Implied consent because the patient did not speak
Involuntary consent because the EMT initiated the request
Substitute consent because the EMT explained the procedure
questions.explanation: A clear informed action can express consent; expressed consent need not be spoken.

questions.question: Which situation describes an emancipated minor rather than another basis for providing care to a minor?
choices: A minor legally treated as an adult for consent under applicable law
A teacher acting in place of an unavailable parent
A child receiving immediately necessary care when a parent cannot be reached
A parent authorizing treatment for a child from another location
questions.explanation: Emancipation concerns the minor’s legal status; emergency doctrine and substitute authority are different routes to consent.

questions.question: A child has a life-threatening injury. A parent cannot be reached promptly and no authorized decision maker is present. Which approach best fits the consent requirement?
choices: Provide immediately necessary care under implied consent
Delay care while dispatch continues trying to reach a parent
Ask an adult bystander to authorize care as a substitute parent
Treat the child’s agreement as adult consent regardless of legal status
questions.explanation: Necessary emergency care can proceed under implied consent when timely authorization is unavailable.

questions.question: A restrained patient becomes cyanotic and struggles to breathe. Scene safety can be maintained while the crew reassesses. What should take priority?
choices: Address airway and breathing and correct the restraint-related hazard
Check restraint security before changing the position
Begin rapid transport and defer restraint changes until arrival
Wait for medical control to authorize reassessment
questions.explanation: A new breathing compromise requires immediate assessment and correction of a potentially lethal restraint hazard.

questions.question: A patient offers to sign a refusal form before hearing the suspected problem, risks, or alternatives. What should the EMT do next?
choices: Explain the concerns and alternatives and assess understanding
Obtain the patient and witness signatures, then give return precautions
Call medical control with the stated refusal before discussing it with the patient
Document the patient’s words and treat the signed form as completion of refusal
questions.explanation: The refusal must be informed. Counseling and assessment of understanding come before treating the form as a completed refusal.

questions.question: A capable adult continues to refuse after assessment, risk counseling, and indicated medical consultation. Which remaining plan best completes the refusal process?
choices: Reoffer care, give follow-up and return advice, seek signatures, and document findings and discussions
Obtain signatures and record the patient’s refusal without the assessment findings
Give return advice and omit the record because medical control was consulted
Document the assessment and leave without explaining when to seek help
questions.explanation: A completed refusal includes continued encouragement, safety advice, requested signatures, and a record of the full process.

questions.question: An EMT removes a patient’s name from a proposed social-media post. The unusual injury, location, and photograph still identify the patient. No disclosure is authorized. What is the best decision?
choices: Do not post the patient-identifying information
Post because the direct identifier has been removed
Post only to a private group of EMS coworkers
Post if a bystander has already shared footage
questions.explanation: Removing a name does not make otherwise identifiable health information appropriate for unauthorized disclosure.

questions.question: A relative requests an identifiable patient-care report. No patient release or other authorized disclosure basis has been established. What should the EMT do?
choices: Use the agency’s confidentiality process before releasing protected information
Release the report because being related to the patient is sufficient authorization
Release it if the relative promises not to share it
Remove only the patient’s name and release the otherwise identifiable report
questions.explanation: Patient-care information is confidential. A request or a promise does not establish authorization; follow the agency’s release process.

questions.question: A patient with a valid DNR order has a pulse, is breathing, and reports discomfort. No other treatment limitation is identified. Which plan best respects the order?
choices: Provide indicated supportive and comfort care under applicable protocols
Limit care to transport because DNR prohibits active treatment
Withhold oxygen and symptom relief until the patient revokes the DNR
Provide usual care but disregard the DNR if arrest occurs
questions.explanation: A DNR limits resuscitation; it does not by itself prohibit indicated supportive care.

questions.question: A pulseless, apneic adult has no obvious irreversible-death findings. The family presents a document, but the crew cannot determine whether it is an applicable resuscitation-limiting order. What is the best approach?
choices: Follow the resuscitation protocol while seeking prompt medical-control clarification
Withhold CPR while medical control reviews the document
Accept the family’s interpretation and document who supplied it
Set the document aside and make no further effort to clarify it
questions.explanation: An uncertain document requires the applicable verification process. Do not create an unsupported delay in indicated resuscitation while seeking clarification.

questions.question: A patient is unresponsive, apneic, and pulseless. No applicable DNR or obvious irreversible-death finding is identified. Why do these findings not by themselves justify withholding resuscitation?
choices: They establish arrest but do not establish irreversible death
They establish irreversible death once all three occur together
They justify withholding unless a relative requests CPR
They justify withholding once the skin feels cool
questions.explanation: Absent pulse and breathing are arrest findings; withholding requires the applicable protocol’s criteria.

questions.question: Postmortem discoloration appears in the lowest body regions because blood settles with gravity. Which term describes this finding?
choices: Dependent lividity
Rigor mortis
Algor mortis
Putrefaction
questions.explanation: Dependent lividity describes gravitational blood settling and resulting dependent discoloration.

questions.question: An injured patient carries an organ-donor card and needs immediate treatment. How should donor status affect the initial priority?
choices: Provide lifesaving care first and communicate donor information as appropriate
Confirm donation eligibility before beginning treatment
Prioritize transport to a transplant center over the patient’s immediate clinical needs
Use the card as authority to limit resuscitation
questions.explanation: The donor’s own life remains the priority; donor status can be communicated without delaying care.

questions.question: An altered patient wears a bracelet listing a medical condition and an emergency contact. What is the best use of this information?
choices: Use it to guide assessment while continuing care for current threats
Accept the listed condition as the diagnosis and omit other assessment
Complete contact verification before treating immediate threats
Disregard the bracelet until the patient can confirm its accuracy
questions.explanation: Medical identification supplies useful clues but complements current assessment and urgent care.

questions.question: An EMT may perform a procedure under state rules but performs it less carefully than a reasonably competent EMT would. Which distinction applies?
choices: Scope concerns authorization; standard of care concerns expected performance
Scope concerns expected performance; standard of care concerns authorization
State authorization means the standard of care is met whenever the procedure is attempted
A poor outcome alone proves the procedure exceeded scope
questions.explanation: Permission to perform a skill and the expected manner of performing it are separate questions.

questions.question: An off-duty EMT voluntarily begins patient care. A replacement clinician has not yet accepted responsibility. What follows from beginning care?
choices: The EMT must continue appropriate care until an accepted transfer or another lawful end of care
The EMT may leave because there was no initial duty to respond
The patient’s location at an emergency facility ends the EMT’s responsibility automatically
The duty applies only if the EMT is paid for the encounter
questions.explanation: Beginning care creates a responsibility to follow through appropriately, even when the initial assistance was voluntary.

questions.question: Which combination contains the four elements required to establish negligence?
choices: Duty, breach of duty, damages, and causation
Duty, breach of duty, damages, and intent to harm
Duty, breach of duty, consent, and causation
Duty, foreseeable risk, damages, and certification
questions.explanation: Negligence requires a duty, a breach, actual damages, and a causal connection between the breach and damages.

questions.question: A capable adult expressly refuses a nonemergency procedure. No emergency exception or other legal authority applies. The EMT performs it anyway. Which term most directly describes the unauthorized physical contact?
choices: Battery
Assault
False imprisonment
Abandonment
questions.explanation: Battery concerns unauthorized or unlawful physical contact.

questions.question: A crew arrives at the ED, but no appropriate clinician has accepted responsibility for the patient. What should the crew do?
choices: Continue care and arrange an accepted clinical handoff
Leave after delivering a written report to the nursing desk
End care once the patient is inside the receiving facility
Treat an administrative arrival signature as acceptance of clinical responsibility
questions.explanation: Physical arrival or paperwork does not by itself complete the transfer of patient care.

questions.question: Findings raise concern for child abuse during a call. What is the most appropriate response?
choices: Treat current needs, record objective findings, and report through the required process
Delay reporting until the EMT can establish who caused the injuries
Document the concern but rely on another agency to decide whether reporting is needed
Promise confidentiality to encourage disclosure and report only with the family’s permission
questions.explanation: The EMT provides care, documents facts, and follows applicable mandated-reporting requirements rather than trying to prove the case.

questions.question: A capable patient understands the recommended care but declines it for personal religious reasons. The EMT believes the treatment would help. Which response best reflects professional ethics?
choices: Respect the informed choice while explaining options and offering appropriate care
Treat disagreement with the recommendation as proof of impaired capacity
Let the accompanying family override the patient’s informed choice
Continue persuasion until agreement is obtained before recognizing refusal
questions.explanation: Respect for autonomy allows a capable patient to make an informed choice the clinician would not make.

questions.question: An EMT receives a subpoena to testify about a call. Which preparation best supports an accurate professional response?
choices: Notify the service director and legal counsel; review the care record and distinguish memory from recorded facts
Review the report privately without notifying the service’s legal process
Reconstruct missing facts from what usually happens on similar calls
Coordinate testimony with coworkers so every account is identical
questions.explanation: Use the service’s legal process and the record to prepare truthful testimony without inventing or harmonizing facts.

questions.question: During discovery, an EMT receives written questions and later gives oral testimony under oath outside trial. Which terms apply in that order?
choices: Interrogatories; deposition
Deposition; interrogatories
Subpoena; deposition
Interrogatories; trial testimony
questions.explanation: Interrogatories are written discovery questions; a deposition is oral testimony under oath before trial.

questions.question: A combative patient needs care and presents danger to others. Which principle governs involuntary treatment and restraint?
choices: Use applicable legal authority and local protocols, with medical control and law enforcement as indicated
Treat any psychiatric history as automatic authority for forced transport
Use a family request as sufficient authority regardless of the patient’s status
Assume any refusal permits restraint because treatment would be helpful
questions.explanation: Involuntary care and restraint require the applicable legal and protocol framework; diagnosis, family wishes, and disagreement alone are not substitutes.

questions.question: An EMT unlawfully threatens immediate restraint, then physically grabs a capable refusing adult without legal authority. Which terms describe the threat and contact in that order?
choices: Assault; battery
Battery; assault
Abandonment; negligence
Negligence; abandonment
questions.explanation: Assault concerns fear of immediate bodily harm; battery concerns unlawful physical contact.

questions.question: A capable adult refuses transport. No emergency exception or custody authority applies, but the crew confines the patient and carries them away by force. Which legal issue specifically concerns this loss of freedom of movement?
choices: Kidnapping and false imprisonment
Battery
Assault
Defamation
questions.explanation: Unauthorized confinement and forced transport raise false-imprisonment and kidnapping concerns.

questions.question: An injured patient is at a suspected crime scene. Which approach balances care, reporting, and preservation of evidence?
choices: Treat immediate needs, disturb the scene only as required for care, document actions, and follow reporting requirements
Delay lifesaving care until all evidence has been photographed by the crew
Rearrange nearby objects to make the scene easier for investigators to interpret
Avoid documenting moved objects because their original positions may be uncertain
questions.explanation: Patient care remains necessary, while avoidable scene disturbance is limited and relevant findings and actions are documented.

questions.question: Which description correctly distinguishes ethics from applied ethics?
choices: Ethics examines right and wrong; applied ethics incorporates those principles into professional conduct
Ethics incorporates principles into professional conduct; applied ethics examines right and wrong
Ethics addresses health care questions exclusively; applied ethics is a personal code of conduct
Ethics establishes legal permission to perform a skill; applied ethics defines the required technical steps
questions.explanation: Ethics concerns moral duties and ideal professional behavior; applied ethics concerns how principles guide actual conduct.

questions.question: What is abandonment in patient care?
choices: Ending care without consent or transfer to an appropriate provider
Providing emergency care under implied consent
Failing to act exactly as a similar trained provider would
Threatening immediate unlawful physical contact
questions.explanation: Abandonment is termination of care without an appropriate transfer or consent; negligence and assault describe different issues.

questions.question: What does morality describe?
choices: A code of conduct affecting character, conduct, and conscience
The philosophy of right and wrong and professional duties
The application of ethical principles to professional conduct
The ethical questions specific to health care practice
questions.explanation: Morality is a code of conduct. Ethics is the philosophy, applied ethics concerns incorporating principles into conduct, and bioethics addresses health care issues.

questions.question: Which postmortem change consists of muscle stiffening caused by chemical changes within muscle tissue?
choices: Rigor mortis
Dependent lividity
Algor mortis
Putrefaction
questions.explanation: Rigor mortis is postmortem muscle stiffening.

questions.question: An EMT treats an injury sustained during a suspected felony. Which approach to reporting is appropriate?
choices: Check and follow the applicable mandatory-reporting law and agency process
Report only if the patient signs a release of medical information
Wait until a criminal conviction establishes that a felony occurred
Treat ordinary clinical handoff as automatically satisfying every reporting requirement
questions.explanation: Special reporting requirements can include injuries during a felony and vary by state; use the applicable law and process.

questions.question: An EMT assumes that a patient who avoids eye contact is being disrespectful because direct eye contact is expected in the EMT’s own culture. Which communication barrier does this illustrate?
choices: Ethnocentrism
Cultural imposition
Environmental noise
Language difference
questions.explanation: Ethnocentrism means interpreting others through the belief that one’s own cultural values are more important or correct. Eye-contact expectations vary by culture.

questions.question: A patient says, “I feel strange.” The EMT asks, “What do you mean by strange?” Which interviewing technique is the EMT using?
choices: Reflection
Explanation
Clarification
Summary
questions.explanation: Clarification asks the patient to explain an unclear response so the EMT does not assign an unsupported meaning.

questions.question: During the interview, a breathless patient can manage only very brief responses. Which question places the least demand on the patient’s ability to speak?
choices: How has your breathing changed since this morning?
Are you having chest pain?
What treatments have you tried for your breathing?
How does this episode compare with previous episodes?
questions.explanation: A focused closed-ended question permits a brief yes-or-no response. Open-ended questions are useful when the patient can provide more detail.

questions.question: An alert patient is able and willing to answer, but a family member answers each question first. How should the EMT obtain the history?
choices: Complete the interview with the family member, then ask the patient to approve the account.
Ask the family member to answer while the patient supplies only corrections.
Interview the family member separately and use that account as the primary history.
Give the patient the opportunity to answer, then ask the family member for additional information.
questions.explanation: Family can supply valuable information, but an able and willing patient should have the opportunity to answer. Ask others to step aside briefly if needed.

questions.question: During hospital hand-over, the patient still requires assisted ventilation. Which information should the EMT convey first?
choices: The ongoing ventilation requirement and the need for the receiving team to continue it.
The full sequence of events that led the family to call EMS.
The patient’s complete medication list and relevant past illnesses.
The route taken, scene time, and method used to move the patient.
questions.explanation: Immediately convey critical airway, breathing, or circulation support that must continue. History and routine transport details follow without interrupting essential care.

questions.question: An older adult is newly confused and irritable during the interview. Which approach is appropriate?
choices: Compare the behavior with baseline and assess for a medical cause while communicating calmly.
Finish the history with family before evaluating the patient’s new confusion.
Shorten the examination if the patient reports little pain and can still answer questions.
Treat the behavior as an expected age-related communication difficulty unless agitation increases.
questions.explanation: New confusion or irritability should not be assumed to be normal aging. Assess possible medical causes and communicate slowly and patiently.

questions.question: Before a procedure that may briefly hurt, a child asks whether it will hurt. Which response best supports trust?
choices: “Let’s talk about your toy first, and we can discuss the procedure afterward.”
“Your parent can tell you what it feels like while I get started.”
“It may hurt briefly. I’ll explain what I’m doing before I begin.”
“You won’t feel anything because this will be quick.”
questions.explanation: Children should receive honest, age-appropriate explanations before a painful procedure. Familiar objects and family support can help without replacing that explanation.

questions.question: A patient with hearing loss is having difficulty following the interview. Which adjustment should the EMT make?
choices: Increase volume and continue speaking while turning to gather equipment.
Face the patient and speak slowly and distinctly without shouting.
Speak into the patient’s ear at close range so facial position is less important.
Ask a companion to repeat each question while directing your questions toward the companion.
questions.explanation: Facing the patient lets them see the speaker’s lips. Slow, distinct speech supports understanding; shouting can distort speech.

questions.question: A visually impaired patient is able to walk and asks for help reaching the ambulance. Which method is appropriate?
choices: Walk behind the patient and guide by pushing gently between the shoulders.
Walk ahead and give directions from several steps away.
Take the patient’s cane and use it to show the route ahead.
Explain the movement and have the patient place a hand on your arm.
questions.explanation: Explain care and movement, and let a walking patient place a hand on your arm for guidance. Transport mobility aids with the patient.

questions.question: A patient speaks little English, and a professional interpreter is available by phone. How should the EMT obtain the history?
choices: Use the interpreter and ask short, simple questions directed to the patient.
Ask only questions that can be answered by pointing and leave the remaining history for the hospital.
Use a family member for the entire history because a familiar voice is more reliable than a professional interpreter.
Use medical terminology so the interpreter and patient hear the most precise wording.
questions.explanation: A language barrier does not remove the need for a history. A professional interpreter and short, simple questions support accurate communication.

questions.question: Which entry belongs in the objective portion of a SOAP narrative?
choices: “The patient reports dizziness that began after standing.”
“The patient’s spouse reports a previous fainting episode.”
“Blood pressure 92/60 mm Hg; skin pale and cool.”
“Possible circulatory compromise based on the examination.”
questions.explanation: Objective information comes from assessment and measurement, including vital signs and observed physical findings.

questions.question: An EMS agency reviews patient care reports to identify response-time patterns and opportunities to improve care. Which PCR function is being used?
choices: Transfer of responsibility to a receiving clinician
Data collection for continuous quality improvement
Documentation supporting reimbursement for one transport
Communication of one patient’s treatment to the receiving team
questions.explanation: PCR data support continuous quality improvement and research by allowing review of care and operational patterns across calls.

questions.question: Which PCR entry best supports why ambulance transport was medically necessary?
choices: “The family requested an ambulance rather than arranging a ride.”
“The patient was moved on a stretcher to the nearest emergency department.”
“The patient could not safely sit upright and required oxygen during transport.”
“The patient preferred ambulance transport because the crew knew the hospital.”
questions.explanation: Document the patient-specific condition and care needs that made another means of transport unsafe or impossible. Equipment use or patient preference alone does not establish medical necessity.

questions.question: While completing a paper PCR, an EMT discovers that a pulse of 108/min was entered as 180/min. How should the entry be corrected?
choices: Draw one line through 180, initial the correction, and write 108 beside it.
Cover 180 with correction fluid, write 108 over it, and initial the entry.
Erase 180, write 108 in the same space, and retain the original assessment time.
Write 108 elsewhere in the narrative and leave the original pulse entry unchanged.
questions.explanation: A single line preserves the original entry while identifying the correction and the person making it. Accurate, transparent corrections protect the integrity of a legal record.

questions.question: After submitting a PCR, an EMT realizes that a reassessment was performed but not recorded. Which approach preserves the integrity of the report?
choices: Replace the submitted narrative with a new version containing the reassessment.
Ask the receiving nurse to include the reassessment in the hospital record instead.
Enter the reassessment as an addendum with the date and the EMT's initials.
Enter the reassessment under the original narrative date without identifying the addition.
questions.explanation: Accidentally omitted information is added in a section labeled “addendum,” with the date and the provider's initials. This documents the missing information without disguising a later change.

questions.question: A patient declines recommended transport. The PCR includes assessment findings, care provided, the recommendation to go to the hospital, and the patient's signature. Which additional entry documents whether the refusal was informed?
choices: The time the ambulance was dispatched and the time the crew arrived.
The risks of refusing transport that were explained and evidence the patient could make a rational decision.
The name of the witness and the location where the refusal form was signed.
The destination hospital the crew would have used and its estimated travel time.
questions.explanation: Informed-refusal documentation includes the consequences discussed and evidence that the patient could make a rational, informed decision. A signature alone does not document those elements.

questions.question: An EMT treats a patient for a dog bite. How should the crew determine whether a report beyond the routine PCR is required?
choices: Use the patient's preference about involving authorities to decide.
Use the severity of the wound as the deciding criterion.
Leave the reporting decision to the receiving facility after transfer.
Apply the state and local reporting requirements for that incident.
questions.explanation: Dog bites are among incidents that may have special reporting requirements. The applicable state and local requirements determine the reporting obligation; the chapter does not establish a universal local rule.

questions.question: Two ambulance crews cannot reach each other directly by radio. How can a repeater allow them to communicate?
choices: It assigns the next open frequency from a computer-controlled pool.
It receives a signal on one frequency and retransmits it on another using its greater range.
It converts a cardiac monitor's electrical data into a signal for a hospital decoder.
It scans several frequencies and stops to receive an active broadcast.
questions.explanation: A repeater receives a transmission on one frequency and retransmits on another. Its greater power and antenna allow mobile or portable units to communicate beyond their direct range.

questions.question: A radio permits the EMT to speak while the button is pressed and to hear a reply after the button is released. Which operating mode is this?
choices: Duplex
Multiplex
Simplex
Trunking
questions.explanation: Simplex operation is push to talk and release to listen. The distinction concerns how users take turns transmitting and receiving.

questions.question: Medical control gives a treatment order over a noisy connection. The EMT believes the order was heard correctly. What should happen before carrying it out?
choices: Acknowledge receipt and compare the order with the written protocol after treatment.
Document the order as heard and ask the physician to verify it at the hospital.
Repeat the complete order back and obtain confirmation from medical control.
Repeat the treatment name and assume the remaining details match the usual protocol.
questions.explanation: Repeat the order word for word and obtain confirmation. This checks that both parties understand the same instruction before care is provided; clarify anything that does not make sense.

questions.question: The EMT has reported the patient's condition, care and response, priority, and estimated arrival time. Which statement provides the receiving team an opportunity to complete the exchange?
choices: “Do you have any questions or orders?”
“The rest of the information will be available in our PCR.”
“We will provide another report when we enter the emergency department.”
“Please discuss any treatment recommendations with us on arrival.”
questions.explanation: The report concludes by determining whether the receiving facility has additional questions or orders. This allows clarification or further direction before the radio exchange ends.

questions.question: An ambulance arrives at a crash and the crew sees three patients and a blocked access lane. What belongs in the initial arrival message to dispatch?
choices: Individual injury findings, vital signs, and transport priority for each patient.
Treatments completed and the receiving hospital selected for each patient.
The unit's arrival, the visible patient count, and the access problem.
The patient responses to treatment and the expected transport times.
questions.explanation: The crew should report arrival and important obvious scene-size-up details. Patient count and access problems help dispatch coordinate the response while the crew continues assessment.

questions.question: After identifying the unit, an EMT needs to organize the clinical portion of a hospital radio report. Which sequence presents the patient's story coherently?
choices: Age and sex; chief complaint and relevant history; vital signs and findings; care and response.
Care and response; vital signs and findings; age and sex; chief complaint and relevant history.
Vital signs and findings; care and response; chief complaint and relevant history; age and sex.
Chief complaint and relevant history; care and response; age and sex; vital signs and findings.
questions.explanation: The report moves from patient identification and presenting problem to history, assessment findings, and then treatment with the patient's response. This gives the receiver context for the findings and interventions.

questions.question: A radio report describes the patient's initial breathing difficulty and the oxygen treatment given. Which additional detail lets the receiving team judge the patient's response to that care?
choices: Whether the patient had used oxygen before this illness.
The time the crew first reached the patient.
The initial vital signs obtained before oxygen was started.
Changes in breathing and reassessment findings after oxygen was started.
questions.explanation: Response to treatment is demonstrated by changes in the patient's condition and reassessment findings after the intervention. Initial findings and treatment details provide context, but do not establish the response.

questions.question: During handoff, an EMT uses an unfamiliar shorthand expression. The receiving clinician asks what it means. Which response best serves the purpose of medical terminology?
choices: State the finding clearly using words both clinicians understand
Repeat the shorthand because brevity is the primary goal
Substitute another abbreviation without checking whether it is understood
Leave the expression unexplained if it appears in the written report
questions.explanation: Medical terminology supports accurate shared understanding; speed should not take priority over clarity.

questions.question: Which list identifies the four components used to construct medical terms?
choices: Word root, prefix, suffix, combining vowel
Word root, prefix, suffix, abbreviation
Word root, combining vowel, acronym, symbol
Prefix, suffix, abbreviation, anatomic position
questions.explanation: Roots supply the foundation; prefixes and suffixes modify meaning; combining vowels connect components.

questions.question: In nephr/o/pathy, what function does the o perform?
choices: It connects the root to the suffix and eases pronunciation
It changes the organ named by the root
It means disease and supplies the condition
It indicates that the term is plural
questions.explanation: The o is a combining vowel between nephr and -pathy; it does not carry the disease or organ meaning.

questions.question: A patient reports difficulty swallowing but no difficulty speaking. Which term documents the swallowing complaint?
choices: Dysphagia
Dysphasia
Aphasia
Dysuria
questions.explanation: Dysphagia means difficulty swallowing. The similar-looking term dysphasia concerns language or speech, not swallowing.

questions.question: Which interpretation correctly combines nephr and -pathy in nephropathy?
choices: Kidney disease
Kidney enlargement
Kidney inflammation
Liver disease
questions.explanation: Nephr means kidney and -pathy means disease.

questions.question: Which term means enlargement of the liver?
choices: Hepatomegaly
Hepatitis
Nephromegaly
Hepatopathy
questions.explanation: Hepat- identifies the liver and -megaly means enlargement.

questions.question: A patient’s record describes polydipsia. Which complaint does that term identify?
choices: Excessive thirst
Frequent urination
Difficulty swallowing
Low blood glucose
questions.explanation: Polydipsia describes excessive thirst, not frequent urination or low blood glucose.

questions.question: Bleeding has stopped after a hemorrhage-control intervention. Which term describes that result?
choices: Hemostasis
Hemolysis
Hematemesis
Hemiplegia
questions.explanation: Hemostasis describes the stopping of bleeding.

questions.question: A clinician documents hyperemesis. Which meaning is supported by hyper- and emesis?
choices: Excessive vomiting
Absence of vomiting
Painful swallowing
Difficulty urinating
questions.explanation: Hyper- means excessive and emesis means vomiting.

questions.question: A forearm wound is halfway between the elbow and wrist. Which term describes the wound’s location relative to the wrist?
choices: Proximal
Distal
Medial
Lateral
questions.explanation: The wound is nearer the trunk than the wrist, so it is proximal to the wrist. Medial and lateral describe a different relationship: distance from the midline.

questions.question: In anatomic position, how is the sternum located relative to the patient’s right shoulder?
choices: Medial
Lateral
Proximal
Distal
questions.explanation: The sternum is closer to the body’s midline than the shoulder, so it is medial to the shoulder.

questions.question: Which paired description correctly relates the head, chest, and feet?
choices: The head is superior to the chest; the feet are inferior to the chest
The head is inferior to the chest; the feet are superior to the chest
The head is lateral to the chest; the feet are medial to the chest
The head is distal to the chest; the feet are proximal to the chest
questions.explanation: Superior and inferior describe relationships toward the head and feet, respectively.

questions.question: Which synonym pairing is correct?
choices: Anterior = ventral; posterior = dorsal
Anterior = dorsal; posterior = ventral
Anterior = superior; posterior = inferior
Anterior = medial; posterior = lateral
questions.explanation: Anterior/ventral refers to the front; posterior/dorsal refers to the back.

questions.question: A skin abrasion overlies an injury farther inside the tissue. How are the injuries related?
choices: The abrasion is superficial to the deeper injury
The abrasion is distal to the deeper injury
The abrasion is lateral to the deeper injury
The abrasion is inferior to the deeper injury
questions.explanation: Superficial/deep describes distance from the skin surface.

questions.question: You face a patient with an injury on their right upper arm and another on their right wrist. Which description correctly uses the patient’s side and the upper-arm injury’s relation to the wrist?
choices: Right arm; proximal to the wrist
Left arm; proximal to the wrist
Right arm; distal to the wrist
Left arm; distal to the wrist
questions.explanation: Anatomic side belongs to the patient. The upper arm is nearer the trunk than the wrist, so it is proximal.

questions.question: A patient has one injury on the palm of the hand and another on the sole of the foot. Which pair describes these surfaces in that order?
choices: Palmar; plantar
Plantar; palmar
Dorsal; plantar
Palmar; dorsal
questions.explanation: Palmar names the palm surface; plantar names the sole.

questions.question: An assessment notes a finding on the left side of the chest only. A later finding involves both sides. Which terms describe the extent in that order?
choices: Unilateral; bilateral
Bilateral; unilateral
Medial; lateral
Proximal; distal
questions.explanation: Unilateral means one side; bilateral means both sides.

questions.question: A patient moves an arm away from the body’s midline and then brings it back toward the midline. Which movements occur in that order?
choices: Abduction; adduction
Adduction; abduction
Flexion; extension
Extension; flexion
questions.explanation: Abduction moves away from the midline; adduction moves toward it.

questions.question: Which pair correctly identifies the plane separating front from back and the plane separating upper from lower portions?
choices: Frontal/coronal; transverse/horizontal
Transverse/horizontal; frontal/coronal
Sagittal/median; transverse/horizontal
Frontal/coronal; sagittal/median
questions.explanation: The frontal/coronal plane separates front and back; the transverse/horizontal plane separates upper and lower portions.

questions.question: The first patient is lying face down; the second is lying face up. Which positions should be documented in that order?
choices: Prone; supine
Supine; prone
Prone; recovery
Recovery; supine
questions.explanation: Prone is face down; supine is face up.

questions.question: A patient is supported with the stretcher back at 45 degrees. Which position is most specific?
choices: Semi-Fowler
High-Fowler
Supine
Prone
questions.explanation: The outline identifies 45-degree back elevation as semi-Fowler and 90-degree elevation as high-Fowler.

questions.question: Which interpretation correctly combines an-, alges, and -ic in analgesic?
choices: Pertaining to the absence of pain
Pertaining to increased pain
Pertaining to painful or difficult movement
Pertaining to the absence of sensation
questions.explanation: An- means without or absence of; alges means pain; -ic means pertaining to.

questions.question: A shortcut symbol is understood by your own crew but is not accepted by other care teams in the service area. What is the best choice for the patient-care report?
choices: Write out the finding in clear terms
Use the symbol and explain it during verbal handoff
Use the symbol only in the narrative section
Use the symbol and add a second familiar abbreviation
questions.explanation: The report should remain understandable across the care team, including readers who were not present at handoff.

questions.question: A report states LUQ pain. Where is the pain documented?
choices: Left upper quadrant
Left lower quadrant
Right upper quadrant
Right lower quadrant
questions.explanation: LUQ means left upper quadrant.

questions.question: What does CPR stand for in a patient-care report?
choices: Cardiopulmonary resuscitation
Cardiopulmonary respiration
Cardiac pressure recording
Cardiovascular pulse reassessment
questions.explanation: CPR is the abbreviation for cardiopulmonary resuscitation.

questions.question: When using the suffix-first approach to interpret a term with a prefix, root, and suffix, what sequence is used?
choices: Suffix → prefix → root
Suffix → root → prefix
Prefix → root → suffix
Root → prefix → suffix
questions.explanation: Begin with the suffix and work backward, then interpret the prefix and root.
tags: Method of breaking down an unfamiliar term

questions.question: What is a word root in medical terminology?
choices: The main part of a word that carries its basic meaning
A component placed before the root to modify meaning
A component placed after the root to modify meaning
A vowel used to connect word components
questions.explanation: The root carries the basic meaning; a prefix precedes it, a suffix follows it, and a combining vowel links components.

questions.question: What does distal mean when describing an extremity?
choices: Farther from the trunk or point of attachment
Closer to the trunk or point of attachment
Closer to the body’s midline
Closer to the body’s surface
questions.explanation: Distal describes distance away from attachment; proximal, medial, and superficial describe the other relationships.

questions.question: A patient is lying on the left side. How should the EMT interpret anatomic descriptions of the patient’s body?
choices: Use the standing, forward-facing position with palms forward as the reference
Use the patient’s current position as the reference for anterior and posterior
Reverse left and right when approaching the patient from the front
Use palms facing backward as the reference for the upper limbs
questions.explanation: Anatomic position provides a consistent reference regardless of the patient’s actual position.

questions.question: An image separates structures toward the front of the body from structures toward the back. Which plane produces that division?
choices: Coronal
Sagittal
Transverse
Midsagittal
questions.explanation: A coronal plane separates anterior and posterior portions.
